content.text:
The course registration app is finished in `/work`, and the start page is `index.html`. It uses plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step, and you can open it directly from disk or through any static file server. I tested it in headless Chromium: all four pages are reachable from the navigation bar, there were no console errors, and the automated accessibility checker (axe-core, WCAG 2.2 AA rules plus best-practice rules) found 0 violations on every page and in every state I tested.

**Files**
- `index.html`, `catalog.html`, `register.html`, `profile.html`: the four pages.
- `css/styles.css`: all styles.
- `js/data.js`: 16 sample courses across 7 departments, each department with its own color.

  - Dropdown filters for department, level, credits and open seats, plus a "Clear filters" button.
  - Course cards showing how many seats are left.
  - The result count is announced to screen readers, with a short delay so it doesn't speak on every keystroke.
- **Register:**
  - A form for student details, year of study and course checkboxes. Full courses and courses you've already registered for can't be selected.
  - A side panel shows your selected courses and total credits; the limit is 18.
  - A confirmation pop-up shows everything before you submit.
  - "Register" buttons on the catalog cards open this page with that course already ticked.
- **My Profile:** your student details, a term summary, and a table of registered courses with a total-credits row. Each course has a "Drop" button that asks for confirmation first.

**Accessibility**
- **Navigation and structure:**
  - A "skip to main content" link and correct page landmarks.
  - The current page is marked in the navigation bar.
  - On mobile, a "Menu" button opens the navigation and tells screen readers whether it's open.
- **Form:**
  - Every field has a label, and hints and error messages are linked to their fields.
  - Invalid fields are marked for screen readers.
  - When you submit with mistakes, a list of the errors appears and gets focus. Each item links to its field, and the page title starts with "Error:".
- **Pop-ups:** they keep keyboard focus inside, close with Escape, and return focus to the button that opened them. After you confirm, focus moves to the success message.
- **Table:** it has a caption and column and row headers, scrolls sideways with the keyboard, and turns into stacked rows on small screens.
- **Course cards:** buttons and links include the course name for screen readers (for example, "Register for CS 340 Web Accessibility & Design").
- **Visual:**
  - All colors meet WCAG AA contrast, and focus outlines are clearly visible.
  - Color is never the only way information is shown.
  - Animations are turned off for users who prefer reduced motion, and the high-contrast mode in Windows is supported.
- **Responsive:** there is no sideways scrolling at 375px wide. On very narrow screens (320px) the Menu button moves to its own line, aligned to the right.

**Testing**
The automated run covered navigation, search and filters, an invalid submission, the confirmation pop-up (cancel with Escape, then confirm), registering, and dropping a course. Each page was checked at desktop and mobile widths. Automated checks can't catch everything, so it's still worth a quick manual check with a real screen reader.

When I first ran the tests from local files, the console showed errors from the accessibility checker, which can't load the stylesheet over `file://`. Over a local web server the console was clean, so those errors don't come from the app.

The test tools were installed in `/tmp`, not in the project folder. I haven't committed anything; the new files are untracked in git.
